hints: Each die independently shows a value from 1 through 6.
Build the probability distribution of the sum one die at a time.
Add the probabilities for sums in the requested inclusive interval.
analogy: Each new die shifts the existing sum distribution by one of six equally likely faces.
example: For one die, probability of a sum from 2 to 4 is 3/6=0.5.
algorithm: Initialize dp[0]=1. For each die, distribute each dp[s]/6 to dpNew[s+1..s+6]; sum dp[a..b] and print with required precision.
correctness: The transition lists all six equally likely outcomes for the next independent die, so each final sum receives exactly its probability mass.
complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n) space for n dice.
